spans.name: Hadean
spans.summary: A molten, meteor-battered young Earth. Oceans form and life may begin.

spans.name: Archean
spans.summary: Microbes rule an oxygen-free world and build the first reefs (stromatolites).

spans.name: Proterozoic
spans.summary: Oxygen floods the air, complex cells appear and the first animals emerge.

spans.name: Phanerozoic
spans.summary: The eon of visible life — shells, forests, dinosaurs, flowers and us.

spans.name: Paleoproterozoic
spans.summary: The Great Oxidation Event rusts the oceans; the first complex cells evolve.

spans.name: Mesoproterozoic
spans.summary: The 'boring billion' — slow, steady evolution, including the first multicellular algae.

spans.name: Neoproterozoic
spans.summary: Snowball Earth glaciations, then the first animals in the Ediacaran seas.

spans.name: Paleozoic
spans.summary: Life explodes in the sea, then conquers the land: forests, insects and four-legged animals.

spans.name: Mesozoic
spans.summary: The Age of Reptiles: dinosaurs, pterosaurs, the first mammals, birds and flowers.

spans.name: Cenozoic
spans.summary: The Age of Mammals, grasslands, ice ages and, finally, humans.

spans.name: Tonian
spans.summary: The supercontinent Rodinia breaks apart; early algae and amoebae diversify.

spans.name: Cryogenian
spans.summary: Snowball Earth: ice may have reached the equator.

spans.name: Ediacaran
spans.summary: Strange soft-bodied creatures, the first large animals, carpet the sea floor.

spans.name: Cambrian
spans.summary: The Cambrian explosion: eyes, shells, trilobites and nearly every animal body plan.

spans.name: Ordovician
spans.summary: Seas teem with life; the first plants creep onto land.

spans.name: Silurian
spans.summary: Jawed fish appear, coral reefs spread and plants grow stems.

spans.name: Devonian
spans.summary: The Age of Fishes. The first forests rise and fish take their first steps on land.

spans.name: Carboniferous
spans.summary: Giant swamp forests (our coal) and huge insects in oxygen-rich air.

spans.name: Permian
spans.summary: The supercontinent Pangaea. Ends with the worst extinction ever.

spans.name: Triassic
spans.summary: Life recovers. The first dinosaurs, pterosaurs and mammals appear.

spans.name: Jurassic
spans.summary: Giant long-necked sauropods, Stegosaurus, Allosaurus and the first birds.

spans.name: Cretaceous
spans.summary: Flowers bloom, T. rex and Triceratops roam — until an asteroid strikes.

spans.name: Paleogene
spans.summary: Mammals inherit the Earth: early whales, horses and primates.

spans.name: Neogene
spans.summary: Grasslands spread, apes thrive and our ancestors stand upright.

spans.name: Quaternary
spans.summary: Ice ages, mammoths, the rise of Homo sapiens and the invention of farming.

events.name: Earth forms
events.summary: Dust and rock around the young Sun clump together into our planet.

events.name: Oldest signs of life
events.summary: Chemical traces and microbial mats in ancient rocks of Greenland and Australia.

events.name: Great Oxidation Event
events.summary: Cyanobacteria pump oxygen into the air for the first time — poison to many microbes, fuel for future life.

events.name: Snowball Earth
events.summary: Glaciers may have covered the whole planet, perhaps twice.

events.name: Cambrian explosion
events.summary: In a geological blink, most major animal groups appear in the fossil record.

events.name: Plants reach land
events.summary: Moss-like plants start greening the bare continents.

events.name: End-Ordovician extinction
events.summary: Ice ages and falling seas wipe out about 85% of marine species.

events.name: Late Devonian extinction
events.summary: Oxygen-starved oceans kill most reef builders and armoured fish.

events.name: The Great Dying
events.summary: Massive Siberian volcanoes kill ~90% of all species — the worst extinction in Earth's history.

events.name: End-Triassic extinction
events.summary: Volcanism clears the way for dinosaurs to dominate.

events.name: Asteroid impact (K–Pg)
events.summary: A 10 km asteroid hits Mexico. All non-bird dinosaurs vanish, opening the world to mammals.

events.name: Farming begins
events.summary: Humans start domesticating plants and animals — evolution by human choice.
